params.place: on the map: the whole of Australia, the fence line across it

moments.what: Australia's border traces round and its flag fills it
a light runs along the fence line from the coast
a fence-post sign pops up with the length on it
the camera pushes in on the line
question marks pop on both sides of the line

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What is Australia's 5,614 kilometre fence keeping out?

params.place: on the map: the fence's first post on the cliffs of the Great Australian Bight

moments.what: the camera arrives at the south end of the line
cliffs rise along the coast and waves break below
the first panel of wire mesh stands up
a height marker climbs the post to the figure
a small figure walks up beside the wire
the figure looks up at the top wire

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It starts on the cliffs of the south coast: wire 180 centimetres high, taller than you.

params.place: on the map: the fence across the desert of South Australia

moments.what: a patrol truck sets off along the fence and the odometer appears
the truck drives north, the camera following
the land around the line warms to desert red
a salt pan opens beside the truck
SOUTH AUSTRALIA writes on beside the line

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: From there it runs north, across the red dunes and salt pans of the South Australian desert.

params.place: on the map: the corner where South Australia, New South Wales and Queensland meet

moments.what: the truck reaches the bend
the truck turns east along the line
a corner post marks the three states
the truck rolls past the post
NEW SOUTH WALES writes on below the line
the camera pulls back as the line climbs north
QUEENSLAND writes on above the line

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then it swings east to the corner where three states meet, crosses into New South Wales, and climbs north through Queensland,

params.place: on the map: the fence's last post among the farms of the Darling Downs

moments.what: the odometer rolls to the full length
the truck pulls up at the last post
green paddocks and a farmhouse appear around the end
a windmill turns by the farmhouse
DARLING DOWNS writes on

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: until it finally stops among the farms of the Darling Downs.

params.place: on the map: the whole continent, split by the line

moments.what: the camera pulls back to the whole continent
the fence line flashes bright
Australia's outline glows
the land on the two sides tints in two colours
a question mark drops on the north-west side
a question mark drops on the south-east side

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now look at the map again. One wire splits the land into two sides. So what lives on each side of it?

params.place: on the map: sheep country in the south-east, inside the fence

moments.what: the camera slides to the south-east
SHEEP COUNTRY writes on
a first flock of sheep pops onto the grass
more flocks pop up across the land
the sheep put their heads down to graze
tufts of grass sway

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: To the south and east is sheep country: flock after flock, grazing on open grass.

params.place: on the map: a stretch of the early wire in the outback, rabbits running at it

moments.what: an old stretch of wire stands on the line
the wire turns sepia like an old photograph
workers' posts stand along it
rabbits pour across the land towards it
rabbits slip under and through and a red cross stamps on the wire
the camera pulls back
a question mark pops over the line

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It began in the eighteen-eighties as a fence against rabbits, and against rabbits it failed. So why keep it?

params.place: on the map: dingo country in the outback, north and west of the fence

moments.what: the camera crosses the wire to the other side
the outback side lights up orange
a dingo trots up to the wire, big
WILD DOG writes on its tag
more dingoes roam across the outback
DINGO COUNTRY writes on to the north
paw prints run off to the west

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Because on the other side lives the hunter of sheep: the dingo, Australia's wild dog, roaming the north and west.

params.place: on the map: the fence line being built, close, with workers on it

moments.what: the camera drops close onto the line
two workers in old hats lift the wire higher
a roll of wire unrolls along the line, joining two stretches
a post drops into the ground
another post drops in
posts march off along the line
the dingo on the far side stops at the wire
the dingo turns away

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So the wire was raised and joined into one fence, post by post, kilometre after kilometre, to keep the dingo out.

params.place: on the map: two lengths of wire stretched out over the continent

moments.what: a ribbon of wire stretches across the map with today's length
a second ribbon stretches out far past it
the second ribbon's length counts up
both ribbons pulse
a dingo stands at the end of the long ribbon
the camera pushes in on the one dingo

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And it used to be even longer: over 8,000 kilometres of wire, all to stop one hungry wild dog.

params.place: on the map: the whole of Australia again, the fence line across it

moments.what: a sheep pops on the south-east side
a dingo pops on the north-west side
a pointer swings between them
the camera pulls back to the whole continent
a light runs along the fence line
Australia's border lights up
the frame settles on the hook's map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Sheep side or dingo side: which would you pick? Now you know what one wire across Australia is keeping out.
